headline: Alvia Asset Partners sees CSL as attractively valued at ~15x FY27 earnings with risk/reward skewed to buyers at current levels
reasoning: Chris Scarpato believes the market has overcorrected on CSL, moving from pricing it as a market darling to pricing it for significant terminal issues. He acknowledges CSL's Vifor acquisition was a poor capital allocation decision due to inadequate due diligence, overpaying, and material patent risk, but argues these problems are now largely in the price. The core blood plasma business remains a comfortable oligopoly with no new entrants in 20–25 years and CSL is the world's largest blood plasma fractionator. The flu vaccine business faces near-term headwinds from the anti-vaccination stance of the US administration under RFK but remains a top-three global player. With new/returning management under Gordon Naylor focusing on core operations and a CEO recruitment process underway, Scarpato is confident green shoots are emerging, and at approximately 15x FY27 earnings the risk/reward is in buyers' favour.
quote: We think at current levels, yes, we think so. Bringing back Gordon Naylor, who has been a CSL veteran, he has got the tough job of obviously effectively running a strategic review on that business. I think the biggest thing for them is the blood plasma business where you could see their commercial execution has slipped up. They've had some R&D misses as well. It's very much a focus back on the core. The market has assessed Vifor as a dud and so it's a matter of managing that business but making sure they get the most out of their key businesses. We're rather confident that the green shoots are there. The market has seen those earnings downgrades and we're quietly confident that at current levels, you're sort of paying 15 times FY27 earnings. We think the risk reward is on buyers at around current levels.
episode_title: Why Chris thinks it could be time to buy CSL

headline: Alvia Asset Partners views Australian healthcare as undervalued and shunned relative to AI-driven market enthusiasm, presenting an opportunity
reasoning: Chris Scarpato argues that Australian healthcare has been left behind in a market preoccupied with identifying AI winners and losers. He sees the sector as offering high-quality global franchises that are currently undervalued, and suggests that a turn may be beginning for the beaten-down local healthcare space.
quote: In a market that feels infatuated with trying to find the next AI winner or loser, I feel like, we feel like as a business here at Alvear, that healthcare has very much been shunned or left behind, at least on the local market.
episode_title: Why Chris thinks it could be time to buy CSL
